{{Short description|1967 book by Kazimierz Ajdukiewicz}}
{{about|the book|the mathematical concept referred to as "Polish logic"|Polish notation}}{{More citations needed|date=April 2026}}
{{italic title}}

'''''Polish Logic''''' is an anthology of papers by several authors—[[Kazimierz Ajdukiewicz]], [[Leon Chwistek]], [[Stanislaw Jaskowski]], Zbigniew Jordan, [[Tadeusz Kotarbinski]], [[Stanisław Leśniewski]], [[Jan Łukasiewicz]], [[Jerzy Słupecki]], and Mordchaj Wajsberg—published in 1967 and covering the period 1920&ndash;1939. The work focuses on the contributions of Polish [[logician]]s, more particularly, [[mathematical logic]]ians, to [[modern logic]].<ref>{{cite book |last=Łukasiewicz |first=Jan |translator-last=Wojtasiewicz |translator-first=Olgierd |title         =Elementy logiki matematycznej |trans-title=Elements of Mathematical Logic |series=International Series of Monographs in Pure and Applied Mathematics |volume=31 |year=1963 |orig-year=1929 |publisher=[[Pergamon Press]] |location= |language=pl-PL |pages=xi, 124 |lccn=63010013 |url=https://archive.org/details/elementsofmathem0031ukas|author-link=Jan Łukasiewicz}}</ref>
